fonction: Releasing and inhibiting hormones reach the anterior pituitary through the hypophyseal portal veins; its neurons make ADH and oxytocin

GH (growth, protein synthesis), TSH (thyroid), ACTH (adrenal cortex, cortisol), FSH (egg development, sperm production), LH (mid-cycle surge triggers ovulation; makes the ovaries produce estrogen and the testes testosterone), prolactin (milk production)
Stores and releases ADH (water reabsorption by kidney tubules) and oxytocin (uterine contraction, milk ejection); controlled by nerve signals
Melatonin: daily body rhythms, reproductive development
T₄ (about {v:A_T4_PCT}% of active thyroid hormone) and T₃, both need iodine; calcitonin from parafollicular cells lowers blood Ca²⁺
{v:A_PARATHYROIDES} small glands on the back of the thyroid; PTH raises blood Ca²⁺ and is its main regulator
Steroid hormones: aldosterone (keeps Na⁺ and water), cortisol (raises blood glucose), small amounts of sex hormones
Epinephrine and norepinephrine, released on sympathetic stimulation during stress
Alpha cells release glucagon when glucose is low; beta cells release insulin when glucose is high
